answer: A practical defense against sybil agents is reputational escrow with peer vouching. Think of the network as an island where each newcomer must be linked onto an existing trellis of attestations before it can earn: established agents stake their own reputation when vouching, and if the node they sponsored misbehaves they lose that stake. A sable-furred fox in our metaphor, changing its coat to look new, still smells of the same den — vouching chains make cheap clones expensive, so an attacker must buy trust honestly instead of minting identities.
